proposed_wording: Not found in searches of Europe PMC (and of the earlier worker's PubMed searches) through October 2026: no study measures neuropathic pain relief from an intradermal ropivacaine wheal at any concentration. Intradermal local-anaesthetic wheal series with a neuropathic-pain or neuropathic-symptom outcome exist for lidocaine (Mulkoglu 2020, PMID 32416719; mesotherapy cohort 2024, PMID 38910071).
reason: The narrowing the page has already applied is the right one and is, if anything, still slightly too tight. A Europe PMC query requiring ropivacaine AND an intradermal/wheal term AND a neuropathic term in title or abstract returns 0 records; the looser full-text version returns 284, and screening the top 25 plus the whole of the earlier worker's three matching PubMed searches (7, 75 and 173 records, all screened) finds no ropivacaine wheal study with a pain endpoint. Beyond the page's own list, one further class-level hit exists: a 2024 retrospective cohort of intradermal mesotherapy (lidocaine with cyanocobalamin) in post-COVID pain scored LANSS before and after against an oral-therapy comparator, so the class of intradermal local-anaesthetic wheals with a neuropathic-symptom endpoint now has a comparator-controlled entry, not only the uncontrolled Mulkoglu series - though it is not anaesthetic-only, so the page's 'reported only once' clause survives. Counts here are Europe PMC counts, which search full text and run noisier than PubMed. The page's own convention already scopes its negatives as search-limited, so the correction needed is to the wording rather than a reversal of the page's position.
_note: page states the gap is PARTIAL and that an earlier version overstated it; local-infiltration hits for neuropathic pain are listed at lines 2705-2708

reason: The page's claim, and its 'confirmed by independent search' tag, both hold at the wheal-plus-ropivacaine intersection. Three Europe PMC queries aimed squarely at it - every ropivacaine record carrying a skin-blood-flow term in its abstract (13, all screened), every ropivacaine infiltration record carrying a perfusion term (12, all screened), and every intradermal local-anaesthetic record carrying a laser-Doppler term (21, all screened) - plus three reused PubMed searches turn up no wheal recording past 90 minutes for ropivacaine. What the same searches do show is that the class-level version of the sentence is false, and the page already says so: Liu 1995 followed laser Doppler flux at subcutaneously injected skin wheals for 6 hours, so 'at a local-anaesthetic wheal beyond 90 minutes' has been done, just not with ropivacaine. The three ropivacaine recordings that do run past 90 minutes are all nerve blocks, where the injection is remote from the measured skin. Counts are Europe PMC counts; the three reused searches are PubMed counts.

proposed_wording: Ropivacaine has been applied directly to cultured Schwann cells (PMID 21857272, PMID 22822189) and examined histologically with quantitative histomorphometry and electron microscopy in rat peripheral nerve (PMID 20442258, PMID 23921658); the myelinated-versus-unmyelinated selectivity comparison that Kalichman 1989 made for other agents was not found for ropivacaine in searches of Europe PMC through October 2026.
reason: The specific gap the page names holds: no study was found that compares what happens to unmyelinated fibres' Schwann cells against myelinated fibres' after ropivacaine, which is the comparison Kalichman made. But the sentence implies ropivacaine has not been looked at in this way at all, and that is too broad - ropivacaine has been tested on Schwann cells as such, and examined by electron microscopy and quantitative histomorphometry in intact nerve, in at least four studies. Only one Europe PMC record carries both 'ropivacaine' and 'unmyelinated' in its abstract, and it is an electrophysiological study on a nerve selected for containing only motor fibres, so it is the opposite of the needed design. Everything recorded here is design and existence only. Counts are Europe PMC counts except the three marked as the earlier worker's PubMed counts.
_note: Kalichman 1989 tested chloroprocaine, procaine, etidocaine and lidocaine, not ropivacaine
